#### One query, two clocks — stack and heap at every step

**What is being answered.** Why a streaming query's clock and its update mode are both properties of the query text — as two query functions over the same rows.

`runTumble(clock)` takes the clock as a **parameter**. There is no second code path for processing time: step 2 shows the same line producing bucket 0 or 240 for id 7 depending on one argument. In SQL that argument is three characters.

`sinkNeeds(r)` reads only `r.mode`, which `runFilter` and `runTumble` set from their own shape — so "does my sink need UPSERT?" is answerable from the query before anything runs.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch08-sql-memory/ch08-sql-memory.svg" alt="One query, two clocks — stack and heap at every step, 4 steps showing stack and heap" width="980">

<details>
<summary><b>Step 1 of 4</b> — a filter produces facts, which nothing can revise</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch08-sql-memory/frames/step-01.svg" alt="Step 1: a filter produces facts, which nothing can revise" width="980">

`e.v > FILTER_V` is decided from the row alone — no later row can change whether id 2 matched. That is why the mode is APPEND-ONLY, and it is readable from the query shape rather than measured: a `WHERE` has no state to revise.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — the clock is a PARAMETER, not a second code path</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch08-sql-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: the clock is a PARAMETER, not a second code path" width="980">

For id 7, `b` is 240 with `clock` = "pt" and 0 with "et" — 2 windows apart. One argument, and the row lands somewhere else entirely. In SQL that argument is three characters of the query text.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — so 3 of the 4 buckets hold different sums</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch08-sql-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: so 3 of the 4 buckets hold different sums" width="980">

Read the two heap rows against each other at bucket 0: 19 and 15. Both Results came from the same function over the same rows. Neither is a bug, and nothing in the engine could prefer one.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — and the mode decides what the sink must support</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch08-sql-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: and the mode decides what the sink must support" width="980">

`sinkNeeds` reads only `r.mode`, which was set by the query shape — so the sink contract is derivable before the pipeline runs. `facts` needs INSERT; `byEvent` needs UPSERT, because window [12:00, 12:02) will go from 15 to 19.

</details>
